spanish: Todos los días yo ___ a las siete.
english: Every day I get up at seven.
explanation_or_example: Yo is the subject and also the one getting up, so the pronoun matches it: me. Without me, levanto means I lift something.

spanish: ¿Tú ___ por la mañana o por la noche?
english: Do you shower in the morning or at night?
explanation_or_example: Tú showers yourself, so the reflexive pronoun is te, matching the -as ending. Se is for él, ella, usted or ellos.

spanish: Mi padre ___ antes de desayunar.
english: My father shaves before breakfast.
explanation_or_example: Mi padre shaves himself, so afeitarse needs se for él. Afeita alone means he shaves someone else.

spanish: Nosotros ___ a las once entre semana.
english: We go to bed at eleven during the week.
explanation_or_example: Nosotros put ourselves to bed, so the pronoun is nos. Acostamos alone means we put someone else to bed.

spanish: Los niños ___ las manos antes de comer.
english: The children wash their hands before eating.
explanation_or_example: Los niños wash their own hands, so lavarse with se. Spanish says las manos, not sus manos, because se already shows whose hands.

spanish: ¿A qué hora ___ tú normalmente?
english: What time do you normally wake up?
explanation_or_example: Tú wakes yourself up, so despertarse takes te. Despiertas alone means you wake someone else.

spanish: Ella ___ muy rápido por la mañana.
english: She gets dressed very quickly in the morning.
explanation_or_example: Ella dresses herself, so vestirse needs se. Viste alone means she dresses someone else.

spanish: Yo ___ los dientes tres veces al día.
english: I brush my teeth three times a day.
explanation_or_example: Yo brushes my own teeth, so me cepillo. Spanish says los dientes, not mis dientes, because me already shows whose they are.

spanish: Mi hermana ___ en el coche de camino al trabajo.
english: My sister puts on her make-up in the car on the way to work.
explanation_or_example: Mi hermana does her own make-up, so maquillarse with se. Maquilla alone means she does someone else's make-up.

spanish: Vosotros ___ después del partido, ¿verdad?
english: You all shower after the match, right?
explanation_or_example: Vosotros always pairs with os, matching the -áis ending: os ducháis. Se is for ellos or ustedes.

spanish: Cuando hace frío, yo ___ un abrigo.
english: When it's cold, I put on a coat.
explanation_or_example: Putting un abrigo on yourself is ponerse, so me pongo for yo. Pongo un abrigo would mean you put the coat somewhere.

spanish: Al llegar a casa, mi madre ___ los zapatos.
english: When she gets home, my mother takes off her shoes.
explanation_or_example: Taking off your own clothes, here los zapatos, is quitarse, so se quita for ella. Quita alone means she removes something from someone else.

spanish: Nosotros ___ en el mar todos los veranos.
english: We swim in the sea every summer.
explanation_or_example: Bañarse en el mar means going for a swim, and nosotros takes nos. Bañamos alone means we bathe someone else, like a baby.

spanish: ¿Ustedes ___ temprano los domingos?
english: Do you get up early on Sundays?
explanation_or_example: Ustedes takes the same pronoun as ellos: se levantan. Without se, levantan means you lift something.

spanish: Tú siempre ___ delante del espejo.
english: You always comb your hair in front of the mirror.
explanation_or_example: Delante del espejo shows you are combing your own hair, so peinarse with te for tú. Peinas alone means you comb someone else.

spanish: Mis abuelos ___ muy pronto.
english: My grandparents go to bed very early.
explanation_or_example: Mis abuelos is ellos, so se, and acostarse changes o to ue: se acuestan. Acostan is not a Spanish form.

spanish: Yo ___ el pelo con una toalla.
english: I dry my hair with a towel.
explanation_or_example: Drying your own hair is secarse, so me seco for yo. Spanish says el pelo, not mi pelo, because me already shows whose.

spanish: Pablo ___ para la fiesta durante una hora.
english: Pablo spends an hour getting ready for the party.
explanation_or_example: Arreglarse para la fiesta means getting yourself ready, and Pablo is él, so se. Arregla alone means he fixes something.

spanish: ¿Tú ___ antes o después de desayunar?
english: Do you get dressed before or after breakfast?
explanation_or_example: Tú takes te, and vestirse changes e to i in this form: te vistes. Vestes is not a Spanish form.

spanish: Los domingos nosotros no ___ hasta las diez.
english: On Sundays we don't wake up until ten.
explanation_or_example: Nosotros takes nos, and despertarse keeps its e in the nosotros form: nos despertamos. The ie change only happens in stressed stems.

spanish: Ayer yo ___ a las seis para coger el tren.
english: Yesterday I got up at six to catch the train.
explanation_or_example: Ayer marks a finished past action, and yo got up, so me levanté. The pronoun still comes before the verb in the preterite.

spanish: Anoche los niños ___ muy tarde.
english: Last night the children went to bed very late.
explanation_or_example: Los niños put themselves to bed, so se acostaron. Acostaron alone would mean they put someone else to bed.

spanish: Esta mañana tú no ___ , ¿verdad?
english: You didn't shower this morning, did you?
explanation_or_example: Esta mañana is a finished time, so preterite, and te for tú sits between no and the verb: no te duchaste.

spanish: De niño, yo ___ en el río con mis primos.
english: As a child, I used to swim in the river with my cousins.
explanation_or_example: De niño describes a past habit, so imperfect, and yo needs me: me bañaba. Without me, bañaba means I bathed someone else.

spanish: Usted ___ cada mañana, ¿no?
english: You shave every morning, don't you?
explanation_or_example: Usted takes third-person forms, so the reflexive pronoun is se, not te: se afeita. Te is only for tú.

spanish: Mis hermanas ___ las uñas los viernes.
english: My sisters paint their nails on Fridays.
explanation_or_example: Painting your own nails, las uñas, is pintarse, and mis hermanas is ellas, so se pintan. Pintan alone means they paint something.

spanish: Ella ___ la cara con agua fría.
english: She washes her face with cold water.
explanation_or_example: Washing your own face, la cara, is lavarse, so se lava for ella. Lava alone means she washes something else.

spanish: Yo siempre ___ las gafas para leer.
english: I always take my glasses off to read.
explanation_or_example: Taking off your own glasses, las gafas, is quitarse, so me quito for yo. Quito alone means I take something away.

spanish: Nosotros ___ de blanco para la boda.
english: We are dressing in white for the wedding.
explanation_or_example: Nosotros takes nos, and vestirse keeps its e in the nosotros form: nos vestimos. The i change only happens in stressed stems.

spanish: Cada noche, antes de dormir, mi hijo ___ los dientes.
english: Every night, before going to sleep, my son brushes his teeth.
explanation_or_example: Mi hijo brushes his own teeth, so cepillarse with se. Cepilla alone means he brushes something else, like the dog.

spanish: ¿Ustedes ___ en la primera fila?
english: Are you sitting in the front row?
explanation_or_example: Ustedes takes the same pronoun as ellos: se. Without se, sientan means you seat someone else.

spanish: El perro ___ a la puerta cuando oye el timbre.
english: The dog goes up to the door when it hears the doorbell.
explanation_or_example: Acercarse a la puerta means moving yourself toward it, and el perro is él, so se. Acerca alone means it brings something closer.

spanish: Yo ___ siempre al lado de la ventana.
english: I always sit next to the window.
explanation_or_example: Yo takes me, and sentarse changes e to ie: me siento. Sento is not a Spanish form.

spanish: Cuando ve una araña, mi hermano ___ corriendo.
english: When he sees a spider, my brother runs away from it.
explanation_or_example: Mi hermano moves himself away, so alejarse with se. Aleja alone needs an object: he moves something away.

spanish: Cuando pasa una ambulancia, nosotros ___ a un lado.
english: When an ambulance goes by, we move to one side.
explanation_or_example: Apartarse a un lado means moving yourself aside, and nosotros takes nos. Apartamos alone needs an object: we move something aside.

spanish: El gato ___ debajo de la cama.
english: The cat hides under the bed.
explanation_or_example: Debajo de la cama is where the cat hides itself, so esconderse with se. Esconde alone needs an object, like esconde la pelota.

spanish: ¿Por qué no ___ tú un rato en el sofá?
english: Why don't you lie down on the sofa for a while?
explanation_or_example: Lying down en el sofá is tumbarse, and tú takes te. Tumbas alone means you knock something down.

spanish: Mis vecinos ___ a Valencia el mes que viene.
english: My neighbours are moving to Valencia next month.
explanation_or_example: Mudarse a Valencia means moving house, and mis vecinos is ellos, so se mudan. Mudan alone means they change or shed something.

spanish: Cuando entra el profesor, los alumnos ___ de la silla.
english: When the teacher comes in, the students stand up from their chairs.
explanation_or_example: Levantarse de la silla means standing up, and los alumnos is ellos, so se levantan. Levantan alone means they lift something.

spanish: Mi abuelo ya no ___ mucho por la casa.
english: My grandfather doesn't move around the house much any more.
explanation_or_example: Mi abuelo is the one moving around, so moverse with se. Mueve alone needs an object, like mueve la mesa.

spanish: Yo ___ la vuelta cuando oigo mi nombre.
english: I turn around when I hear my name.
explanation_or_example: Darse la vuelta, turning yourself around, needs the pronoun, and for yo it is me. Doy la vuelta means you turn something else over.

spanish: Los niños ___ a la piscina sin miedo.
english: The children jump into the pool without fear.
explanation_or_example: Tirarse a la piscina means jumping in yourself, and los niños is ellos, so se tiran. Tiran alone means they throw something.

spanish: ¿Vosotros ___ delante o detrás?
english: Are you all sitting at the front or at the back?
explanation_or_example: Vosotros takes os, and sentarse keeps its e in the vosotros form: os sentáis. The ie change only happens when the stem is stressed.

spanish: Ella ___ a la ventana para ver la calle.
english: She leans out of the window to look at the street.
explanation_or_example: Asomarse a la ventana means leaning out to look, and ella takes se. Asoma alone means something starts to show, like el sol asoma.

spanish: Ayer, al ver el perro, yo ___ despacio.
english: Yesterday, when I saw the dog, I went up to it slowly.
explanation_or_example: Ayer marks a finished action, so preterite, with me for yo. Before é, the c becomes qu: me acerqué.

spanish: El coche ___ delante del semáforo.
english: The car stops in front of the traffic light.
explanation_or_example: El coche stops itself, so detenerse with se. Detiene alone needs an object: la policía detiene al ladrón.

spanish: Cuando hace sol, nosotros ___ en la playa.
english: When it's sunny, we lie down on the beach.
explanation_or_example: Lying down en la playa is tumbarse, and nosotros takes nos. Tumbamos alone means we knock something down.

spanish: Mi hija ___ en el agua aunque está fría.
english: My daughter gets into the water even though it's cold.
explanation_or_example: Getting yourself en el agua is meterse, and mi hija is ella, so se mete. Mete alone needs an object: she puts something in.

spanish: Tú ___ demasiado al fuego.
english: You get too close to the fire.
explanation_or_example: Moving yourself closer, al fuego, is acercarse, and tú takes te. Acercas alone means you bring something closer.

spanish: El año pasado mis padres ___ al campo.
english: Last year my parents moved to the countryside.
explanation_or_example: El año pasado is a finished time, so preterite, and moving house is mudarse: se mudaron. Mudaron alone means they changed something.

spanish: Mi madre ___ mucho cuando llego tarde.
english: My mother worries a lot when I arrive late.
explanation_or_example: Mi madre is the one who feels worried, so preocuparse needs se. Without it, preocupa means she worries someone else.

spanish: Yo ___ mucho en las reuniones largas.
english: I get very bored in long meetings.
explanation_or_example: Yo is the one who gets bored in las reuniones largas, so aburrirse with me. Aburro alone means I bore other people.

spanish: Los niños ___ mucho en el parque.
english: The children have a lot of fun in the park.
explanation_or_example: Los niños is ellos, so se, and divertirse changes e to ie: se divierten. Diverten is not a Spanish form.

spanish: Mi jefe ___ cuando llegamos tarde.
english: My boss gets angry when we arrive late.
explanation_or_example: Mi jefe is the one who gets angry, so enfadarse with se. Enfada alone means he makes someone else angry.

spanish: ¿Tú ___ cuando subes la montaña?
english: Do you get tired when you climb the mountain?
explanation_or_example: Tú is the one who gets tired, so cansarse takes te. Cansas alone means you tire someone else out.

spanish: Nosotros ___ mucho de verte.
english: We are very glad to see you.
explanation_or_example: Alegrarse de means being glad about something, here de verte, and nosotros takes nos. Alegramos alone means we cheer someone up.

spanish: Mi hermana pequeña ___ con las tormentas.
english: My little sister gets scared during storms.
explanation_or_example: Asustarse con las tormentas means getting scared by them, and mi hermana is ella, so se. Asusta alone means she scares someone.

spanish: Hoy yo ___ un poco cansado.
english: Today I feel a bit tired.
explanation_or_example: Sentirse plus an adjective like un poco cansado describes how you feel, and needs me for yo. Siento alone takes a noun: siento frío.

spanish: ¿Cómo ___ usted después de la operación?
english: How do you feel after the operation?
explanation_or_example: Usted takes third-person forms, so sentirse becomes se siente. Te sientes is the tú form.

spanish: Romeo y Julieta ___ en una fiesta.
english: Romeo and Juliet fell in love at a party.
explanation_or_example: Romeo y Julieta fell in love themselves, which is enamorarse: se enamoraron. Enamoraron alone would mean they made someone else fall in love.

spanish: Cuando veo una película triste, yo ___ fácilmente.
english: When I watch a sad film, I get emotional easily.
explanation_or_example: Una película triste moves you, so emocionarse with me for yo. Emociono alone means I move someone else.

spanish: Mis padres ___ al ver la casa tan limpia.
english: My parents were surprised to see the house so clean.
explanation_or_example: Al ver marks the moment they felt surprise, so preterite, and mis padres felt it themselves: se sorprendieron.

spanish: Después de una ducha caliente, yo siempre ___ .
english: After a hot shower, I always relax.
explanation_or_example: After una ducha caliente yo relaxes, which is relajarse, so me relajo. Relajo alone means I relax something, like a muscle.

spanish: ¿Por qué ___ vosotros tan rápido?
english: Why do you all get angry so quickly?
explanation_or_example: Vosotros always takes os, matching the -áis ending: os enfadáis. Se is for ellos or ustedes.

spanish: Mi abuela ___ cuando la visitamos.
english: My grandmother is happy when we visit her.
explanation_or_example: Mi abuela is the one who feels happy, so alegrarse with se. Alegra alone means she cheers someone else up.

spanish: Nosotros ___ por el examen de mañana.
english: We are worried about tomorrow's exam.
explanation_or_example: Preocuparse por means worrying about something, here por el examen, and nosotros takes nos. Preocupamos alone means we worry someone else.

spanish: Ellos ___ en clase de matemáticas.
english: They get bored in maths class.
explanation_or_example: Getting bored en clase is aburrirse, and ellos takes se. Aburren alone means they bore other people.

spanish: Yo nunca ___ con mis amigos.
english: I never get angry with my friends.
explanation_or_example: Enfadarse con means getting angry with someone, here con mis amigos, so me for yo. Enfado alone means I make someone angry.

spanish: Ella ___ cuando habla en público.
english: She gets embarrassed when she speaks in public.
explanation_or_example: Speaking en público embarrasses her, which is avergonzarse, so se. The stem changes o to üe: se avergüenza.

spanish: ¿Tú ___ en la fiesta de anoche?
english: Did you have fun at the party last night?
explanation_or_example: Anoche is a finished time, so preterite, with te for tú. In the preterite the tú stem stays divert-: te divertiste.

spanish: Cuando era pequeño, yo ___ con los payasos.
english: When I was little, I used to get scared of clowns.
explanation_or_example: Cuando era pequeño sets a past habit, so imperfect, and yo got scared myself: me asustaba. Asustaba alone means I scared others.

spanish: Mi novio ___ por cualquier broma.
english: My boyfriend takes offence at any joke.
explanation_or_example: Ofenderse por means taking offence at something, here por cualquier broma, so se. Ofende alone means he offends someone else.

spanish: Los turistas ___ de caminar bajo el sol.
english: The tourists get tired of walking in the sun.
explanation_or_example: Cansarse de means getting tired of something, here de caminar, and los turistas is ellos, so se cansan.

spanish: Con esta música, yo ___ enseguida.
english: With this music, I cheer up straight away.
explanation_or_example: Con esta música yo cheers up, which is animarse, so me animo. Animo alone means I cheer someone else up.

spanish: Ustedes ___ cuando escuchan su voz.
english: You calm down when you hear her voice.
explanation_or_example: Ustedes calm down themselves, so tranquilizarse takes se, the same pronoun as ellos. Tranquilizan alone means you calm someone else.

spanish: Ya es tarde; nosotros ___ de la fiesta.
english: It's late; we're leaving the party.
explanation_or_example: Leaving a place, de la fiesta, is irse: nos vamos. Vamos alone means we go somewhere, as in vamos a la fiesta.

spanish: ¿Vosotros ___ de la cena del sábado?
english: Do you all remember Saturday's dinner?
explanation_or_example: Remembering something takes acordarse de, here de la cena, with os for vosotros. Acordar alone means to agree on something.

spanish: Los dos países ___ un alto el fuego.
english: The two countries agreed on a ceasefire.
explanation_or_example: Un alto el fuego is something agreed, and agreeing on something is acordar, with no pronoun. Se acordaron would mean they remembered.

spanish: Estaba tan cansado que ___ en cuanto me senté.
english: I was so tired that I fell asleep as soon as I sat down.
explanation_or_example: En cuanto marks the moment sleep started, which is dormirse: me dormí. Dormí alone describes sleeping, as in dormí ocho horas.

spanish: Anoche ___ ocho horas seguidas.
english: Last night I slept eight hours straight.
explanation_or_example: Ocho horas measures how long you slept, which is plain dormir: dormí. Me dormí is the moment you fell asleep.

spanish: Mi hermano ___ Javier.
english: My brother is called Javier.
explanation_or_example: Giving a name, here Javier, uses llamarse: se llama means he is called. Llama alone means he calls someone.

spanish: Yo ___ a mi madre todos los domingos.
english: I call my mother every Sunday.
explanation_or_example: A mi madre is the person who gets the call, so plain llamar: llamo. Me llamo is how you give your own name.

spanish: Al final, nosotros ___ en casa porque llovía.
english: In the end, we stayed at home because it was raining.
explanation_or_example: Staying en casa is quedarse, so nos quedamos. Quedamos alone means we arranged to meet.

spanish: Nosotros ___ con Ana a las ocho en la plaza.
english: We're meeting Ana at eight in the square.
explanation_or_example: Quedar con alguien, here con Ana, means arranging to meet, with no pronoun. Nos quedamos con Ana would mean we stay with Ana.

spanish: Antes de salir, yo ___ de todos.
english: Before leaving, I say goodbye to everyone.
explanation_or_example: Saying goodbye to people, de todos, is despedirse de: me despido. Despido alone means I fire someone.

spanish: La empresa ___ a veinte trabajadores.
english: The company laid off twenty workers.
explanation_or_example: A veinte trabajadores is who loses their job, so plain despedir, to fire: despidió. Se despidió de would mean it said goodbye.

spanish: Ana ___ mucho a su madre.
english: Ana looks a lot like her mother.
explanation_or_example: Looking like someone, a su madre, is parecerse a: se parece. Parece alone means seems, as in parece cansada.

spanish: Tu idea me ___ muy interesante.
english: Your idea seems very interesting to me.
explanation_or_example: Muy interesante is an opinion about the idea, so plain parecer, to seem: me parece. Se parece a is for looking like someone.

spanish: Mi hermano y yo ___ muy bien.
english: My brother and I get on very well.
explanation_or_example: Llevarse bien, here muy bien, means getting on well, so nos llevamos. Llevamos alone means we carry or take something.

spanish: Yo siempre ___ paraguas en invierno.
english: I always carry an umbrella in winter.
explanation_or_example: Paraguas is the object you carry, so plain llevar: llevo. Me llevo bien is about getting on with people.

spanish: El niño ___ a comer verduras.
english: The boy refuses to eat vegetables.
explanation_or_example: Refusing to do something, a comer, is negarse a: se niega. Niega alone means he denies something.

spanish: El acusado ___ todo delante del juez.
english: The accused denies everything in front of the judge.
explanation_or_example: Todo is what he denies, a direct object, so plain negar: niega. Se niega a is for refusing to do something.

spanish: Ayer ___ con Luis en el supermercado.
english: Yesterday I ran into Luis at the supermarket.
explanation_or_example: Bumping into someone, con Luis, is encontrarse con: me encontré. Encontré alone means found, as in encontré las llaves.

spanish: Por fin ___ mis llaves debajo del sofá.
english: I finally found my keys under the sofa.
explanation_or_example: Mis llaves is the thing you found, so plain encontrar: encontré. Me encontré con is for running into someone.

spanish: Primero la madre ___ al bebé y después cena.
english: First the mother puts the baby to bed and then has dinner.
explanation_or_example: Al bebé is the person put to bed, so plain acostar: acuesta. Se acuesta would mean she goes to bed herself.

spanish: Yo ___ el coche los sábados.
english: I wash the car on Saturdays.
explanation_or_example: El coche is what gets washed, not you, so plain lavar: lavo. Me lavo is for washing yourself.

spanish: Con la fama, el actor ___ muy arrogante.
english: With fame, the actor became very arrogant.
explanation_or_example: Volverse plus an adjective, here muy arrogante, means to become: se volvió. Volvió alone means he came back.

spanish: Mi padre ___ del trabajo a las seis.
english: My father comes back from work at six.
explanation_or_example: Del trabajo is where he comes back from, so plain volver, to return: vuelve. Se vuelve means he becomes or turns around.

spanish: En esta ciudad es fácil ___ sin un mapa.
english: In this city it's easy to get lost without a map.
explanation_or_example: Sin un mapa you get lost yourself, which is perderse. Perder alone needs an object, like perder las llaves.

spanish: ¿Tú ___ en los detalles?
english: Do you notice the details?
explanation_or_example: Fijarse en, here en los detalles, means to notice, with te for tú. Fijas alone means you fix or set something.

spanish: Mi hermana ___ el próximo sábado.
english: My sister is getting married next Saturday.
explanation_or_example: Mi hermana is the one getting married, which is casarse: se casa. Casa alone means she marries other people, like a judge.

spanish: Mi socio ___ de las cuentas de la empresa.
english: My business partner takes care of the company's accounts.
explanation_or_example: Ocuparse de, here de las cuentas, means taking care of something: se ocupa. Ocupa alone means it takes up space.

spanish: Por la mañana, yo ___ a mis hijos a las siete.
english: In the morning, I wake my children up at seven.
explanation_or_example: A mis hijos is who gets woken up, so plain despertar: despierto. Me despierto would mean you wake up yourself.

spanish: Pedro ___ la mesa antes de cenar.
english: Pedro sets the table before dinner.
explanation_or_example: Poner la mesa, setting the table, is plain poner: pone. Se pone is for putting on clothes or becoming, as in se pone nervioso.

spanish: La reunión fue tan aburrida que Marta ___ antes del final.
english: The meeting was so boring that Marta left before the end.
explanation_or_example: Leaving early, antes del final, is marcharse: se marchó. Marchó alone means it went, as in todo marchó bien.

spanish: Mañana tengo que ___ muy temprano.
english: Tomorrow I have to get up very early.
explanation_or_example: After tengo que the infinitive takes the pronoun on its end, and it must match yo: levantarme. Levantarse would mean him or her.

spanish: Ahora mismo Ana está ___ el pelo.
english: Right now Ana is washing her hair.
explanation_or_example: With está plus a gerund, the pronoun attaches to the end: lavándose, with an accent to keep the stress. It can't sit between está and the gerund.

spanish: Esta noche vamos a ___ pronto.
english: Tonight we're going to go to bed early.
explanation_or_example: After vamos a the pronoun attaches to the infinitive and matches nosotros: acostarnos. Acostarse would point to él, ella or ellos.

spanish: ¿Quieres ___ aquí, al lado de la ventana?
english: Do you want to sit here, next to the window?
explanation_or_example: Quieres is tú, so the infinitive carries te on its end: sentarte. Sentarse would mean someone else.

spanish: Antes de ___ , leo un rato en la cama.
english: Before going to bed, I read for a while in bed.
explanation_or_example: Leo shows the subject is yo, so after antes de the infinitive takes me on its end: acostarme.

spanish: Los niños están ___ ahora mismo.
english: The children are having a shower right now.
explanation_or_example: With están plus a gerund the pronoun attaches to its end: duchándose, with an accent to keep the stress. It can't sit between están and the gerund.

spanish: No puedo ___ con tanto ruido.
english: I can't concentrate with so much noise.
explanation_or_example: No puedo is yo, so the infinitive takes me on its end: concentrarme. Concentrarse would mean él, ella or usted.

spanish: Mi hermano sigue ___ del trabajo.
english: My brother keeps complaining about work.
explanation_or_example: After sigue the gerund carries the pronoun on its end: quejándose. Quejarse is always reflexive, so quejando alone is not possible.

spanish: Nosotros nunca ___ juntos.
english: We never get bored together.
explanation_or_example: Nunca comes before a conjugated verb, and the pronoun goes right before that verb: nunca nos aburrimos. Aburrirnos needs a verb before it.

spanish: Para no ___ , uso el GPS.
english: So as not to get lost, I use the GPS.
explanation_or_example: Uso shows the subject is yo, so after para no the infinitive takes me on its end: perderme.

spanish: ¿Vais a ___ a cenar?
english: Are you all going to stay for dinner?
explanation_or_example: Vais a is vosotros, so the infinitive takes os on its end: quedaros. Quedarse would be for ellos or ustedes.

spanish: Estoy ___ ; salgo en cinco minutos.
english: I'm getting dressed; I'm leaving in five minutes.
explanation_or_example: Estoy is yo, so the gerund takes me on its end, with an accent: vistiéndome. Vestir changes e to i in the gerund.

spanish: Ellos quieren ___ en primavera.
english: They want to get married in spring.
explanation_or_example: Ellos quieren has a third-person subject, so the infinitive keeps se: casarse. Casarnos would mean we get married.

spanish: Usted debe ___ más.
english: You should look after yourself more.
explanation_or_example: Usted takes third-person forms, so the infinitive keeps se: cuidarse. Cuidarte is for tú.

spanish: Tú tienes que ___ un poco.
english: You need to relax a little.
explanation_or_example: Tú tienes que needs te on the end of the infinitive: relajarte. Relajarse would point to él, ella or usted.

spanish: Al ___ , Marta miró el reloj.
english: When she woke up, Marta looked at the clock.
explanation_or_example: Marta is the subject, so after al the infinitive keeps se: despertarse. Despertarme would mean when I woke up.

spanish: Nos estamos ___ para el examen.
english: We're getting ready for the exam.
explanation_or_example: Nos estamos already puts the pronoun before the verb, so the gerund takes no second one: preparando. Preparándonos only works without that nos.

spanish: ¿Te vas a ___ la chaqueta?
english: Are you going to put on your jacket?
explanation_or_example: Te vas a already puts the pronoun before the verb, so the infinitive stays bare: poner. Ponerte would repeat te.

spanish: Me tengo que ___ ya.
english: I have to go now.
explanation_or_example: Me tengo que already puts the pronoun before the verb, so the infinitive stays bare: ir. Tengo que irme is the other correct order.

spanish: Los invitados están ___ porque es medianoche.
english: The guests are leaving because it's midnight.
explanation_or_example: With están plus a gerund the pronoun attaches to the end, and the gerund of ir is yendo: yéndose, with an accent on yén.

spanish: Mis amigos siguen ___ en la fiesta.
english: My friends are still having fun at the party.
explanation_or_example: After siguen the gerund takes se on its end, and divertir changes e to i in the gerund: divirtiéndose.

spanish: Yo no ___ de su nombre.
english: I don't remember his name.
explanation_or_example: Yo no comes before a conjugated verb, so the pronoun goes right before it: no me acuerdo. Acordarme needs a verb like puedo before it.

spanish: Sin ___ , Luis salió de la casa.
english: Without saying goodbye, Luis left the house.
explanation_or_example: Luis is the subject, so after sin the infinitive keeps se: despedirse. Despedirme would mean without me saying goodbye.

spanish: Vosotros estáis ___ de esperar.
english: You all are getting tired of waiting.
explanation_or_example: Vosotros takes os, so the gerund ends in os, with an accent: cansándoos. Cansándose would point to ellos or ustedes.

spanish: Tienes que ___ el cinturón en el coche.
english: You have to put your seatbelt on in the car.
explanation_or_example: Tienes que is tú, so the infinitive takes te on its end: ponerte. Ponerse would point to él, ella or usted.

spanish: Mi hermano siempre ___ nervioso antes de un examen.
english: My brother always gets nervous before an exam.
explanation_or_example: Ponerse plus an adjective like nervioso means to become, and it needs se. Pone alone means he puts something.

spanish: Lo siento, ___ de tu cumpleaños.
english: I'm sorry, I forgot your birthday.
explanation_or_example: Olvidarse de, here de tu cumpleaños, needs the pronoun: me olvidé. Without it you say olvidé tu cumpleaños, with no de.

spanish: De repente, yo ___ cuenta de mi error.
english: Suddenly, I realised my mistake.
explanation_or_example: Darse cuenta de means to realise, and it always needs the pronoun: me di cuenta. Di cuenta alone means I gave an account.

spanish: ¿Tú ___ de la noticia?
english: Did you hear the news?
explanation_or_example: Enterarse de, here de la noticia, means to find out and takes the pronoun: te enteraste. Enteraste alone means you informed someone.

spanish: Los vecinos ___ del ruido todas las noches.
english: The neighbours complain about the noise every night.
explanation_or_example: Quejarse de, here del ruido, means to complain and only exists with the pronoun: se quejan. Quejan alone is not a form you can use.

spanish: Yo no ___ a saltar desde tan alto.
english: I don't dare to jump from so high.
explanation_or_example: Atreverse a, here a saltar, means to dare and is always reflexive: me atrevo. Atrevo on its own is not used.

spanish: Perdona, ___ de número.
english: Sorry, I dialled the wrong number.
explanation_or_example: Equivocarse de número means getting the number wrong, and yo takes me. Before é, the c becomes qu: me equivoqué.

spanish: Mis compañeros ___ de mi acento.
english: My classmates make fun of my accent.
explanation_or_example: Burlarse de, here de mi acento, means to make fun of and always takes the pronoun: se burlan. Burlan alone means they get past something, like a guard.

spanish: Mi tío ___ rico con su empresa.
english: My uncle got rich with his company.
explanation_or_example: Hacerse plus rico means to become, through effort over time: se hizo rico. Hizo alone means made or did.

spanish: Ayer en clase, yo ___ dormido.
english: Yesterday in class, I fell asleep.
explanation_or_example: Quedarse dormido means to fall asleep, and yo takes me: me quedé. Quedé alone means I arranged to meet.

spanish: Yo todavía no ___ al horario español.
english: I still haven't got used to the Spanish timetable.
explanation_or_example: Acostumbrarse a, here al horario español, means getting used to something: me acostumbro. Acostumbro a alone means I usually do something.

spanish: El perro ___ muy bien en el veterinario.
english: The dog behaves very well at the vet's.
explanation_or_example: Portarse bien, here muy bien, means to behave and needs the pronoun: se porta. Porta alone means carries, and is rare.

spanish: Nosotros nunca ___ de acuerdo sobre la película.
english: We never agree on the film.
explanation_or_example: Ponerse de acuerdo means to agree, and nosotros takes nos: nos ponemos. Ponemos alone means we put something.

spanish: Ella ___ de lo que dijo.
english: She regrets what she said.
explanation_or_example: Arrepentirse de, here de lo que dijo, means to regret and is always reflexive: se arrepiente. Arrepiente on its own is not used.

spanish: Yo ___ de hambre; ¿comemos ya?
english: I'm starving; shall we eat now?
explanation_or_example: Morirse de hambre is an everyday exaggeration for being starving, and it needs me. Muero alone sounds like literally dying.

spanish: ¿Cómo ___ tú?
english: What's your name?
explanation_or_example: Asking a name uses llamarse, and tú takes te: te llamas. Llamas alone means you call someone.

spanish: Mi hermana siempre ___ sin batería a mediodía.
english: My sister always runs out of battery by midday.
explanation_or_example: Quedarse sin, here sin batería, means running out of something: se queda. Queda alone means remains or is located.

spanish: ¿Vosotros ___ cuenta del problema?
english: Did you all notice the problem?
explanation_or_example: Darse cuenta de needs the pronoun, and for vosotros it is os: os disteis cuenta. Disteis has no written accent.

spanish: Mi abuela ___ de todo lo que pasa en el barrio.
english: My grandmother finds out about everything that happens in the neighbourhood.
explanation_or_example: Enterarse de, here de todo, means finding out about things, and ella takes se. Entera alone usually means whole.

spanish: Ustedes ___ demasiado, ¿no creen?
english: You complain too much, don't you think?
explanation_or_example: Ustedes takes the same forms as ellos, so quejarse becomes se quejan. Os quejáis is for vosotros.
